The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

hwatch
======

A modern alternative to the watch command. hwatch records command execution results, keeps a history, and can show diffs between runs.

Features
--------
- Records command outputs over time and keeps a history of results.
- Shows differences between executions and supports multiple diff modes.
- Can output results as JSON logs.
- Customizable keybindings and display options.
- Supports ANSI color codes and scrollable output.

Usage
-----
Run hwatch followed by the command you want to monitor. Example:

    hwatch [OPTIONS] [command]...

Common options (user-facing):
- -b, --batch       : Output execution results to stdout instead of the UI.
- -c, --color       : Interpret ANSI color and style sequences in command output.
- -n, --interval    : Seconds to wait between updates (default: 2).
- -l, --logfile     : Write execution history as a JSON log file.
- -h, --help        : Print help.

Configuration
-------------
You can set default options using an environment variable (for example, HWATCH) if you want to always enable certain flags.

Examples
--------
Run a command every 3 seconds:

    hwatch -n 3 command...

Log command outputs to a JSON file:

    hwatch -n 3 -l hwatch_log.json command...

Additional help
---------------
See the manual pages in the man/ directory (if present) or run `hwatch --help` for a full list of options and keybindings.

% hwatch(1) Version 0.3.16 | A modern alternative to the watch command, records the differences in execution results and can check this differences at after.

NAME
====

**hwatch** - A modern alternative to the watch command, records the differences in execution results and can check this differences at after.

SYNOPSIS
========

| **hwatch** \[*options*] *command*

DESCRIPTION
===========

**hwatch** is like *watch* command, repeatedly executes a *command* and displays its output.
However, the output results can be scrolled and displayed.
In addition, the difference of the execution result is recorded with the time stamp, and it can be checked later.
When checking, it is also possible to display the diff with the previous difference together.

If you specify it with options, the execution result can be recorded as a log with json.


Flags
-----

-h, \--help

:   Prints help information


-V, \--version

:   Prints version information


-b, \--batch

:   Output execution results to stdout. NOTE: Operations with TUI are not possible in batch mode.


-B, \--beep

:   beep if command has a change result.


\--border

:   Surround each pane with a border frame


\--with-scrollbar

:   When the border option is enabled, display scrollbar on the right side of watch pane.


\--mouse

:   enable mouse wheel support. With this option, copying text with your terminal may be harder. Try holding the Shift key.


-c, \--color

:   Interpret ANSI colors and style sequences and display in color. It can be changed later by key binding.


-r, \--reverse

:   Display text upside down.


-C, \--compress

:   Compress data in memory. Note: If the output of the command is small, you may not get the desired effect.


-t, \--no-title

:   Hide the UI on start. Use `t` to toggle it.


\--enable-summary-char

:   collect character-level diff count in summary.


-N, \--line-number

:   Show line number.


\--no-help-banner

:   Hide the "Display help with h key" message


\--no-summary


:   disable the calculation for summary that is running behind the scenes, and disable the summary function in the first place.


-x, \--exec

:   Run the command directly, not through the shell. Much like the `-x` option of the watch command.


-O, \--diff-output-only

:   Display only the lines with differences during `line` diff and `word` diff.

\--precise

// Command line definition.
use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command};

pub const ABOUT: &str = "A modern alternative to the watch command, records the differences in execution results and can check this differences at after.";

pub fn build_cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("hwatch")
        .about(ABOUT)
        .version("0.3.19")
        .trailing_var_arg(true)
        .arg(
            Arg::new("command")
                .action(ArgAction::Append)
                .allow_hyphen_values(true)
                .num_args(0..),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("batch")
                .help("output execution results to stdout")
                .short('b')
                .long("batch")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("beep")
                .help("beep if command has a change result")
                .short('B')
                .long("beep")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("border")
                .help("Surround each pane with a border frame")
                .long("border")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("with_scrollbar")
                .help("When the border option is enabled, display scrollbar on the right side of watch pane.")
                .long("with-scrollbar")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("mouse")
                .help("enable mouse wheel support. With this option, copying text with your terminal may be harder. Try holding the Shift key.")
                .long("mouse")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("color")
                .help("interpret ANSI color and style sequences")
                .short('c')
                .long("color")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("reverse")
                .help("display text upside down.")
                .short('r')
                .long("reverse")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("compress")
                .help("Compress data in memory. Note: If the output of the command is small, you may not get the desired effect.")
                .short('C')
                .long("compress")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no_title")
                .help("hide the UI on start. Use `t` to toggle it.")
                .short('t')
                .long("no-title")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("enable_summary_char")
                .help("collect character-level diff count in summary.")
                .long("enable-summary-char")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("line_number")
                .help("show line number")
                .short('N')
                .long("line-number")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no_help_banner")
                .help("hide the \"Display help with h key\" message")
                .long("no-help-banner")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no_summary")
                .help("disable the calculation for summary that is running behind the scenes, and disable the summary function in the first place.")
                .long("no-summary")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("exec")
                .help("Run the command directly, not through the shell. Much like the `-x` option of the watch command.")
                .short('x')
                .long("exec")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("diff_output_only")
                .help("Display only the lines with differences during `line` diff and `word` diff.")
                .short('O')
                .long("diff-output-only")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("after_command")
                .help("Executes the specified command if the output changes. Information about changes is stored in json format in environment variable ${HWATCH_DATA}.")
                .short('A')
                .long("aftercommand")
                .value_name("after_command")
                .action(ArgAction::Set),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("logfile")
                .help("logging file. if a log file is already used, its contents will be read and executed.")
                .short('l')
                .long("logfile")
                .num_args(0..=1)
                .value_name("logfile")
                .action(ArgAction::Set),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("shell_command")
                .help("shell to use at runtime. can also insert the command to the location specified by {COMMAND}.")
                .short('s')
                .long("shell")
                .value_name("shell_command")
                .default_value("sh -c")
                .action(ArgAction::Set),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("interval")
                .help("seconds to wait between updates")
                .short('n')
                .long("interval")
                .value_name("interval")
                .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(f64))
                .default_value("2")
                .action(ArgAction::Set),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("precise")
                .help("Attempt to run as close to the interval as possible, regardless of how long the command takes to run")
                .long("precise")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("limit")
                .help("Set the number of history records to keep. only work in watch mode. Set `0` for unlimited recording. (default: 5000)")
                .short('L')
                .long("limit")
                .value_name("limit")
                .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u32))
                .default_value("5000")
                .action(ArgAction::Set),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("tab_size")
                .help("Specifying tab display size")
                .long("tab-size")
                .value_name("tab_size")
                .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u16))
                .default_value("4")
                .action(ArgAction::Set),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("differences")
                .help("highlight changes between updates")
                .short('d')
                .long("differences")
                .value_name("differences")
                .num_args(0..=1)
                .value_parser(["none", "watch", "line", "word"])
                .default_missing_value("watch")
                .action(ArgAction::Set),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("output")
                .help("Select command output.")
                .short('o')
                .long("output")
                .value_name("output")
                .num_args(0..=1)
                .value_parser(["output", "stdout", "stderr"])
                .default_value("output")
                .action(ArgAction::Set),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("keymap")
                .help("Add keymap")
                .short('K')
                .long("keymap")
                .value_name("keymap")
                .action(ArgAction::Append),
        )
}
EOF

}
EOF

I've written a Rust reimplementation of the provided executable, which turned out to be hwatch 0.3.19. It's committed and `./compile.sh` builds `./executable`. In side-by-side tests the batch mode matched the original exactly, and the interactive screen matched on almost every scenario I tried; the known gaps are listed below.

**How I checked it:** I only ran the original binary and read the bundled docs. I compared outputs automatically:
- **Batch mode (`-b`):** 220+ randomized runs across the four diff modes and their options, compared with timestamps masked. All matched.
- **Interactive screen:** hundreds of scripted key sequences and options in tmux, comparing the full captured screen including colours. Everything matched except the cases below.
- **Command line:** help, version and error messages are byte-identical.

**What's covered:**
- **Command line:** every option, the `HWATCH` environment variable, and the original's crash messages and exit codes in its odd cases (e.g. `-o` with no value, a negative interval).
- **Running commands:** shell, `{COMMAND}` substitution and `-x` mode, interval changes, pause, `--precise`, `-L`, the after-command (`-A`) with `HWATCH_DATA`, and beep.
- **Log files (`-l`):** the JSON log, its quirks (in batch mode it writes the previous result, starting with an empty record), loading an existing log, and the prompts for empty or invalid files.
- **Diffs:** the line and word diffs reproduce the original's exact output, including when it shows word-level highlighting and when it doesn't.
- **Interactive screen:** header, history pane (including the summary view), help and exit dialogs, filtering with keyword/regex and next/previous match, borders and scrollbar, line wrapping and sideways scrolling, mouse, custom key bindings, and terminal resizing.
- **Faithfully reproduced oddities:** for example, the last output line can never be scrolled into view, and the original passes some raw escape codes straight to the terminal.

**Known remaining differences:**
- **Mixed stdout/stderr:** the original combines the two in a random order (usually stderr first), so it sometimes records extra history entries. Mine always puts stderr first.
- **Help window with two keys on one action:** the original lists them in random order.
- **`--enable-summary-char`:** the character counts differ from the original for some larger outputs.
- **`-c` with `-d watch` on coloured output:** small highlight/padding differences remain in some cases.
- **Raw terminal escapes:** where they leak through, the resulting screen corruption can differ slightly.
- **Mouse clicks in the summary view** don't always select the same row after scrolling.
- **Tiny terminals (about 10×3):** the help window renders differently.

**Build dependency:** `compile.sh` builds offline using the crates already in this image's cargo cache, which a fresh clone builds from successfully. If that cache isn't present it falls back to a normal online build, which needs internet. Bundling the crates in the repo would have added about 250MB, so I didn't.
